WIRING.i2c: Plug it into an I2C connector. On most Pixhawk boards the GPS 1 connector carries I2C as well, and an I2C splitter lets several devices share one port.
WIRING.spi: An SPI sensor has to sit on an SPI bus the board brings out for it, usually a connector labelled SPI. A board without one cannot run it.
WIRING.pwm: Connect its PWM line to the pin the PX4 page for your flight controller names for the Lidar-Lite PWM driver.
WIRING.serial: Plug it into the serial connector you pick below; the names are the ones printed on the flight controller. Cross the data lines: the sensor's TX goes to the port's RX, its RX to the port's TX.
WIRING.can: Plug it into a CAN connector, CAN 1 or CAN 2. CAN devices can be chained, and the last one on the bus needs its termination on.
WIRING.board: The driver runs on the port the flight controller's own startup gives it; see the PX4 page for the board.
WIRING.external: Nothing plugs into the flight controller for this: the sensor reaches it over MAVLink, usually from a companion computer.

SENSOR_PRESETS.label: Holybro H-Flow
SENSOR_PRESETS.wiring: Plug it into CAN 1 or CAN 2 with the 4-pin JST-GH cable. It has two CAN connectors, so further CAN devices can be chained behind it; the last device on the bus needs its termination on.
SENSOR_PRESETS.summary: PAA3905E1 optical flow and an AFBR-S50LV85D distance sensor on one board, 0.08 to 30 m, over a single CAN cable.
SENSOR_PRESETS.note: A DroneCAN node rather than a local driver: the autopilot subscribes to the messages it publishes, which is why the CAN stack itself has to be running. Wire it to a CAN port and mount it with the connectors pointing to the back of the vehicle. Set EKF2_OF_POS_X, _Y and _Z to where it sits relative to the centre of gravity. The numbers below are Holybro's own setup values for this module.

SENSOR_PRESETS.label: Matek 3901-L0X
SENSOR_PRESETS.summary: PMW3901 optical flow and a VL53L0X lidar, 0.08 to 2 m, on one UART speaking MSP v2.
SENSOR_PRESETS.unsupported: PX4 has no MSP sensor input. The module speaks MSP v2, which INAV (2.3+) and ArduPilot (4.1+) read and PX4 does not. No parameter on this page can make its flow or distance data reach the estimator. For PX4, use a SPI PMW3901 board or a DroneCAN module.

SENSOR_PRESETS.label: Benewake TFmini-S
SENSOR_PRESETS.wiring: Plug it into a free serial connector, TELEM or GPS, and pick that connector below. The sensor's TX goes to the port's RX and its RX to the port's TX, plus 5 V and ground.
SENSOR_PRESETS.summary: 0.1 to 12 m time-of-flight rangefinder, ±6 cm, on one UART. PX4's TFmini driver uses readings from 0.4 to 12 m.
SENSOR_PRESETS.note: Leave the module in its UART mode; PX4's driver does not read its I2C mode. Any free serial port will do. The baud rate is fixed in the driver, so there is nothing else to set.
params: The TFmini model: the driver's 0.4 to 12 m limits, not the radar's
Use it for height while the vehicle is low and slow
Height below which that range aid is trusted
Measurement noise implied by the datasheet accuracy
The 1 % range-proportional part of that accuracy

SENSOR_PRESETS.wiring: Plug it into a free serial connector, TELEM or GPS, and pick that connector below. The sensor's TX goes to the port's RX and its RX to the port's TX, plus 5 V and ground.

SENSOR_PRESETS.label: Benewake TF03
SENSOR_PRESETS.wiring: Plug it into a free serial connector, TELEM or GPS, and pick that connector below. The sensor's TX goes to the port's RX and its RX to the port's TX, plus 5 V and ground.
SENSOR_PRESETS.summary: 0.1 to 180 m time-of-flight rangefinder, ±10 cm, on one UART. PX4's TFmini driver uses readings from 0.4 to 12 m.
SENSOR_PRESETS.note: The TF03 sends the same 9-byte Benewake frame at 115200 baud as the TFmini, so it runs on the TFmini driver. That driver treats anything past 12 m as out of range, so on PX4 this is a 12 m sensor. Its CAN mode is not read by PX4; keep the module in UART mode.
